episodes: Ep 626: Tesla's Model Y is threatening to become South Korea's top-selling vehicle overall.
Ep 625: Tesla filed four new patents on AI chip math that cut power use in cars while a thirty billion dollar credit line funds the work.

Ep 623: Tesla delivered four hundred eighty six thousand five hundred thirty two vehicles in the third quarter, beating expectations by twenty four thousand.
Ep 623: Tesla delivered four hundred eighty-six thousand five hundred thirty-two vehicles in the third quarter while deploying thirteen point seven gigawatt hours of energy storage.
Ep 622: Tesla's Model Y alone took twenty five point seven percent of all new car registrations in Norway last month.
Ep 621: Tesla has lined up thirty billion dollars in new credit lines to fund expansion in AI, robotics and solar.
Ep 620: A UK safety report flags certain Powerwall 2 units for fire risk and triggers free replacements.
Ep 619: Twenty-eight Tesla Supercharger bays were damaged in the largest attack yet on EV charging sites in Australia.
Ep 618: Tesla Cybercab drew crowds during Hangzhou public tours as interest builds ahead of planned commercial launches in Nevada and Florida.
Ep 617: An Australian Tesla driver has clocked six hundred thousand miles on his Model S with only one battery change.
Ep 616: Tesla Semi production Semi now uses in-house 4680 cells for over 500 miles of range at full load.
Ep 615: Tesla built its first Cybercab using cathode material made at the new Giga Texas plant.
Ep 614: Tesla owners in the US and Australia can now expand their Powerwall 2 systems with the newer Powerwall 3 model.
Ep 613: Tesla China is adding its own intelligent audio algorithm to select Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, turning standard stereo into 360-degree sound via OTA.
Ep 612: Czechia's approval of Tesla FSD opens an early regulatory path even as the ministry had planned to wait for the full EU.
Ep 611: Tesla's Model 3 has topped Spain's car market even as Chinese EVs gain ground.
Ep 610: Tesla's Optimus factory construction is accelerating at Giga Texas ahead of 2027 sales.
Ep 609: Tesla's software update fixed Cybertruck door rattle without a recall or service visit.
Ep 608: Tesla posted record deliveries in Q2 alongside a drop in auto margins to 16.3 percent, showing how volume gains are testing profitability.
Ep 607: NHTSA data shows Tesla's Robotaxi fleet recorded just two minor low-speed scrapes in the latest reporting window.
Ep 606: An Illinois congressman is urging NHTSA to investigate Tesla Autopilot and FSD after videos show drivers asleep.
Ep 605: Tesla's 4680 battery improvements could lift output rates for vehicles and Megapacks at the same time.
Ep 604: Tesla's Roadster teaser image flips to reveal rocket thrusters and the hidden phrase “WHERE WE’RE GOING…” ahead of the October 1 debut.
Ep 603: Tesla is preparing to showcase its dedicated Semi factory on September 24 after years of pilot production.
Ep 602: Tesla landed an $800 million Megapack deal with Zhero for 3 GWh of storage capacity in Italy.
Ep 601: Tesla Powerwalls supplied over 500 MW to California's grid during a heatwave, proving virtual power plant capacity at scale.
Ep 600: Starlink hardware now ships standard in Cybercabs leaving Giga Texas, enabling 4K streaming and gaming on the robotaxi platform.
Ep 599: Tesla needs a record September in China to salvage the quarter after August's 12.4% sales drop.
Ep 598: Tesla's third-generation Megapack production start at Giga Texas adds 50 GWh of annual utility-scale storage capacity.
Ep 597: Fifty Megapacks are now under construction for a 200 MWh storage project in Colorado, extending Tesla Energy's reach into utility-scale grid contracts.
Ep 596: Tesla finalizes its AI5 processor and restarts the Dojo 3 supercomputer using Intel packaging.
Ep 595: The first Cybertruck built with 4680 cells from Tesla's Gulf Coast refinery shows internal battery supply scaling in Texas.
Ep 594: Tesla's Robotaxi fleet reached one million unsupervised miles, giving regulators a concrete data set to evaluate the system.
Ep 593: Model Y's sales leadership in South Korea and Taiwan shows Tesla holding ground in key Asian markets even as rivals push new models.
Ep 592: Installers face six-figure losses after Tesla stopped reporting solar numbers and dropped the Solar Roof.
Ep 591: Tesla Energy's 3 GWh storage deal with Zhero shows grid-scale demand growing independently of vehicle sales.
Ep 590: Tesla's $25 billion 2026 capital budget channels major resources into Optimus scaling.
Ep 589: Tesla's finalized AI 5 processor revives the stalled Dojo 3 supercomputer while clearing volume production at TSMC and Samsung.
Ep 588: Dutch car-sharing firm MyWheels is testing Tesla FSD in its fleet to cut damage claims and explore future autonomous rentals.
Ep 587: Tesla's FSD active users jumped 56 percent to 1.48 million in the second quarter.
Ep 586: Three new semiconductor plants at Giga Texas tighten Tesla's grip on the chips powering its AI systems.
Ep 585: Tesla is extending Dallas Robotaxi hours while its unsupervised fleet grows larger and smarter.
Ep 584: VIN tracking puts Tesla Cybercab production at roughly 2,250 units, underscoring the deliberate pace ahead of the Austin rollout.
Ep 583: Nevada's Tesla Semi factory will test 50,000-unit annual output next month, showing whether long-haul electric trucks can move beyond early fleets.
Ep 582: Global energy storage shipments surged 83% to 303.4 GWh in the first half, pointing to robust growth for Tesla's Megapack operations.
Ep 581: Cybertruck rides at parties are flipping skeptics into instant fans through raw torque.
Ep 580: Researchers turned a Tesla charger flaw into a worm that could hit four EV brands at once.
Ep 579: Nevada's clearance for thousands of robotaxis gives Tesla its clearest path yet to scale an unsupervised fleet beyond California.
Ep 578: Recruitment for Robotaxi operators in Qatar and Saudi Arabia opens Tesla's first Middle East service push.
Ep 577: A Tesla robotaxi in Austin pushed through bollards after repeated stops, testing claims of an impeccable unsupervised record.
Ep 576: Einride's 500-truck Semi order will triple its electric fleet and bring Tesla's heavy-duty trucks to five U.S. states starting next month.
Ep 575: Barclays buying over a million Tesla shares after three quarters of selling shows institutions returning despite mixed market signals.
Ep 574: Tesla's 124-stall San Francisco Supercharger site will test whether open-access sites can maintain uptime while serving mixed fleets.
Ep 573: Tesla marking 10 million EVs produced shows the manufacturing base now in place as pressure builds for the next wave of models.
Ep 572: Tesla plans to idle its Shanghai factory for nearly a month in January as China sales stay weak.
Ep 571: Extended wait times for base Model 3 and Model Y orders point to demand outpacing Tesla's current output capacity.
Ep 570: Tesla's $10.1 billion Texas solar cell plant filing marks its largest single energy manufacturing commitment to date.
Ep 569: Tesla's flush-mounted Starlink antenna on the Cybercab shows the company is betting on satellite connectivity as the backbone for its robotaxi network.
Ep 568: Samsung's accelerated Texas foundry timeline could bring Tesla's AI5 and AI6 chips into mass production earlier than planned.
Ep 567: HW3 Teslas just received FSD v14.1 Lite in the 2026.21.6 update, extending newer autonomy features to older hardware.
Ep 566: Deutsche Bank’s $623 million Tesla stake increase shows institutions still see value after the earnings miss.
Ep 565: Tesla's $10B Texas solar cell factory marks its largest energy hardware bet yet, separate from vehicle production.
Ep 564: Tesla and SpaceX confirmed a $16.8 billion first phase for the Terafab chip plant that will target more annual AI compute output than the entire planet currently produces.
Ep 563: SpaceX's $295 million Megapack order shows Tesla Energy scaling into AI data centers as a distinct revenue stream.
Ep 562: Lemonade’s 50% FSD discount in Tennessee shows insurers beginning to separate supervised autonomy miles from human driving in real pricing.
Ep 561: Tesla's two new Southwest power purchase agreements give its energy business concrete scale while vehicle demand shows regional splits.
Ep 560: Tesla opened a sales and delivery site in Alabama on tribal land to reach customers without changing state franchise rules.
Ep 559: Tesla's first American-made LFP cells are now powering Megapacks rolling out of the factory, tightening the domestic supply chain for utility-scale storage.
Ep 558: Tesla's fleet GNSS correction turns isolated cars into a shared reference network that pins urban positioning back to the road for FSD.
Ep 557: Tesla hit its 10 millionth vehicle produced globally this week at Fremont, a milestone reached just six years after the first million.
Ep 556: Tesla's Cybercab now ships with a factory-integrated Starlink V5 terminal that enables 4K streaming and constant FSD updates during unsupervised rides.
Ep 555: Tesla locked in 90 percent of an Arizona solar-plus-storage project to power its growing AI inference clusters.
Ep 554: Macau’s separate legal framework lets Tesla deliver Grok to owners there while mainland China waits on licensing.
Ep 553: Tesla’s wafer-scale AI design can now isolate an overheating die and keep the rest of the training fabric running without engineer intervention.
Ep 552: Tesla's FSD v14.3.6 now pulls into Sheetz entrances and assigned home spots that previously needed manual driving.
Ep 551: Tesla is sending AI safety operators into Colombia and Chile to oversee the first Robotaxi operations outside North America.
Ep 550: Heavy spending on AI, robots and robotaxis is squeezing Tesla's profits even as revenue climbs to a record.
Ep 549: NHTSA's engineering analysis of FSD on 3.2 million vehicles puts Tesla's camera-only system under final scrutiny before any recall decision.
Ep 548: Starlink V5's roof integration in the Cybercab requires a full redesign of thermal paths and pressure vents that would otherwise limit robotaxi uptime.
Ep 547: Tesla's first Semi Megacharger station in California opens the door to commercial long-haul electric trucking economics.
Ep 546: Tesla's LFP batteries retained 93.34% capacity after 62,000 miles, beating nickel packs and shifting long-term ownership math.
Ep 545: Franz von Holzhausen receiving the first protected Model S Signature unit shows Tesla still values its design heritage even as focus shifts to new platforms.
Ep 544: Tesla opens its first public Megacharger in California, unlocking 1.2 MW speeds for Semi fleets.
Ep 543: Tesla’s Model Y robotaxi fleet in Texas grew 50 percent in one day, marking the first visible test of scaled unsupervised operations.
Ep 542: Tesla posted its best second quarter ever as the energy business spiked sharply higher.
Ep 541: Tesla's European FSD fleet passed 50 million kilometers in under three months, handing regulators in Germany and France the real-world data they have been waiting for.
Ep 540: Tesla's Fremont factory teardown signals the shift from legacy vehicles to Optimus production scale.
Ep 539: Tesla's new patent lets GPUs pull only the exact frames needed for training, cutting wasted decode time at petabyte scale.
Ep 538: Fremont's 46-day teardown of the original Model S and X line frees factory space for Optimus production cells.
Ep 537: Tesla's patented breathing glass roof could cut hot-weather range loss by actively managing cabin climate where the sun hits hardest.
Ep 536: A US judge's approval of the $1.5 million SEC settlement ends Musk's personal liability in the 2022 Twitter disclosure case.
Ep 535: Tesla's Gulf Coast lithium refinery will become North America's largest while cutting emissions more than 30 percent versus hard-rock methods.
Ep 534: NHTSA's plan to drop mandatory brake pedals opens a path for robotaxis built without driver controls from day one.
Ep 533: Optimus now targets mass production at Fremont by end of 2026 with a long-term goal of one million units annually.
Ep 532: Strict lease terms left one driver facing $2,141 in wear-and-tear charges after returning her Tesla.
Ep 531: A 379,000-mile 2019 Model 3 in Canada still shows strong battery health, giving owners concrete data on long-term pack durability.
Ep 530: Tesla posted its fourth-best quarter ever with 480,126 deliveries, but the stock still dropped 7.5 percent.
Ep 529: Tesla's new winter heat patent turns the compressor into a deliberate boiler to protect range when ambient temperatures crash.
Ep 528: Tesla plans to add 1,000 workers at its German Gigafactory as June registrations climb in multiple European markets.
Ep 527: Rows of new Teslas waiting in Japan signal a stronger Q3 start than recent quarters showed.
Ep 526: Texas regulators just cleared 84 Tesla robotaxis, the largest permitted autonomous fleet yet and the first real test of scaled FSD operations.
Ep 524: NHTSA ending its power steering probe on 376,000 Teslas clears one regulatory overhang for the company.
Ep 523: Japan's EV subsidies just slashed the price of a base Model 3 to under $20,000 starting next month.
Ep 522: Tesla's dry-electrode patent adds a protective coating to PTFE binder particles to stop lithium ions from breaking them down inside the cell.
Ep 521: Cybertruck becomes the only 2026 pickup to earn IIHS Top Safety Pick+ after avoiding every pedestrian collision in daytime and nighttime tests.
Ep 518: SpaceX’s first senior unsecured notes offering marks a shift from equity-heavy funding for its rocket and satellite work.
Ep 517: The week's biggest developments, pulled together — what actually moved, why it matters, and what to watch next.
Ep 516: Hundreds of Cybercabs parked at Giga Texas show production may outpace the regulatory path for unsupervised operation.
Ep 515: Tesla's new lowest-priced Cybertruck trim begins deliveries this week at $59,990.
Ep 514: Tesla's FSD update will remember owners' parking preferences and reduce repeated manual inputs during daily drives.
Ep 513: New Jersey legislation could block true driverless cars, and Tesla is urging owners there to push back before it advances.
Ep 512: Tesla’s Dojo networking patents move packet recovery into hardware so the training fabric keeps running even when Ethernet drops frames.
Ep 511: ABF Freight's order of two Tesla Semis puts the first long-range electric trucks into California linehaul service with routes extending to Reno.
Ep 510: The week's biggest developments, pulled together — what actually moved, why it matters, and what to watch next.
Ep 509: Tesla's foldable Superchargers heading to Europe could cut installation time for new sites.
Ep 508: Tesla Model Y just topped all foreign vehicle registrations in Japan for May.
Ep 507: ABF Freight's order of two Tesla Semis for California routes moves the electric truck from prototype to paid freight work.
Ep 506: Denmark's FSD Supervised approval extends the system to four European countries and shows how regulatory progress can outpace fleet deployment elsewhere.
Ep 505: Tesla's push for a 5,000-vehicle robotaxi fleet in Las Vegas sets the first concrete test of large-scale unsupervised operations.
Ep 504: China's 22% Tesla sales rebound in May signals demand recovery after a two-month slump.

Ep 502: Tesla's import of a Chinese-built Premium AWD Model 3 into Canada for under $50,000 tests whether cross-border sourcing can offset domestic production constraints.
Ep 501: Tesla ending free Supercharging for new Model 3s on June 15 removes a key ownership perk just as buyers weigh total costs against rivals.
Ep 500: Tokyo's new EV incentives could nearly halve Tesla prices in the capital region.
Ep 499: Tesla's new interior accent lights now turn red to warn of blind-spot vehicles, giving drivers a direct visual cue without glancing at mirrors.
Ep 498: Halifax gets its first Supercharger site under construction, extending the network into Atlantic Canada for the first time.
Ep 497: China's 39% jump in Tesla wholesale volume signals resilient demand amid intensifying EV rivalry.
Ep 496: Tesla's FSD approval in Estonia opens public roads in a third European country after Lithuania and the Netherlands.
Ep 495: Tesla's May registrations more than doubled in Spain and surged across other European markets, signaling a clear demand rebound.

Ep 491: The 2026 Model Y became the first vehicle ever to pass the US government's new advanced driver assistance safety tests.
Ep 490: A Teslarati editor is running FSD v14.3.3 hands-free across 122 miles of turnpike without touching the wheel once.

Ep 486: Tesla's dry cathode process could slash battery production costs as Elon confirms the tech's potential.
